result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You came to the hospital on 14 October 2026 after a fall at home. You hit your head. You did not lose consciousness.

An X-ray of your right hip shows no fracture. A CT scan (a detailed X-ray scan) of your head shows no bleeding inside the head.

Your blood pressure was 142/80 lying down. It was 108/66 standing. This shows postural hypotension. This means your blood pressure drops when you stand up.

Amlodipine may be making your blood pressure drop when you stand. This is possible, not certain.

## What you need to do
1. Stop taking amlodipine 10 mg.
2. Stand up slowly.
3. Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand.
4. Wait for a letter from the Falls Prevention Clinic. You have been referred. They will write to you with an appointment.

Your GP (family doctor) will recheck your blood pressure, lying and standing, in 4 weeks.

## Dates and medicines
- 14 October 2026: you were seen at the hospital.
- In 4 weeks: your GP will recheck your lying and standing blood pressure.
- Amlodipine 10 mg: stop.
- All other medicines: continue. The letter gives no names or doses.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What does postural hypotension mean for me?
- Why might amlodipine cause my blood pressure to drop?
- What will happen at the Falls Prevention Clinic?

## When to get urgent help
If you get a worsening headache, vomiting, confusion or drowsiness in the next few days, call 999 or go to A&E (the hospital emergency department).

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
